source.title: Identifying Mislabeled Data using the Area Under the Margin Ranking
source.authors: Geoff Pleiss; Tianyi Zhang; Ethan R. Elenberg; Kilian Q. Weinberger

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary information are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports test error across label-noise levels, but does not measure whether networks fit random labels or their training error on corrupted sets. Its citation of the random-label result is not an experiment testing that result.
record.gate_note: The paper cites zero training error on random labels as prior work. Its own noisy-label experiments report test error after training or data removal, not training error on corrupted labels. Only the test-error component of V4 is measured; rows do not establish perfect training fit.
record.test_reason: Standard-training noise sweeps test V4's test-error component. Training-logit trajectories also bear on V6's distinction between learning clean and noisy labels. Perfect training fit and population-level learning order are not established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly summarizes the authors' main conclusion: AUM and threshold samples identify mislabeled data, and removing flagged samples often improves classification. Its assertion that no claim version is tested is too strong: the standard-training controls bear on V4's test-error component, and the logit trajectories bear on V6's different-learning-dynamics component.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a noisy-label identification and data-removal method; it does not reproduce the cited random-label training experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that AUM identification struggles with highly systematic asymmetric noise at higher noise levels; data augmentation is not required for AUM cleaning to improve test error in the reported CIFAR10 comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: AUM identification precision/recall, architecture correlations, threshold sensitivity, and test-error improvements after data removal measure detection or mitigation performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-margin statistics can identify harmful or mislabeled examples and enable dataset cleaning.

record.code_released: https://github.com/cleanlab/cleanlab (the text names a package, but does not state this URL); package: pip install aum
record.problems: Training error on noisy or random labels is not reported. The random-label fitting statement is cited prior work, not a result of this study. Larger datasets use a single trial without confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the paper's own test-error results concern removing identified examples from noisy datasets and do not measure the behaviors named by V1–V6. Values for standard training on corrupted labels are not rows for V4 because training fit is unreported and the task is synthetic label corruption rather than completely random labeling.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence time across corruption levels.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.
Perfect training fit at every corruption level; the fully randomized endpoint. Experiments cover intermediate corruption levels.
Whether regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing regularization preserves clean-label generalization.
Population-level learning times establishing that clean patterns precede eventual noise memorization; completely random-label training.

missing.what: Standard-training test-error rows across uniform corruption levels for CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Tiny ImageNet. The record explicitly excludes these, but its rationale incorrectly requires training-fit evidence before recording the tested test-error component of V4.
missing.locator: Section 4.2, Tables 1–2, Standard rows; Appendix A for training details.

missing.what: Qualitative clean-versus-mislabeled logit trajectories: Figure 2 averages 50 examples per plotted group; clean assigned logits dominate alternatives, whereas mislabeled assigned logits remain below ground-truth logits for most of training. Record the qualitative result without inventing learning-time values.
missing.locator: Figure 2 and Section 3, Area Under the Margin Ranking.

record.verdict_notes: Missing training-error measurements are untested components, not evidence against the claims. AUM scores alone do not establish learning order; the V6 verdict rests on the reported logit trajectories. Purposefully constructed threshold samples and improvements from cleaning do not establish random-label memorization.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks fit completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, their test error at chance, and whether this occurs without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption rises.
Training on shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The study reports test error across corruption levels but does not report training error or verify perfect training fit at each level.
Whether regularization or augmentation prevents fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, or whether these are learned differently over training.

relationships.condition: Standard ResNet-32 training with 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% uniform label corruption.
relationships.reason: Tables 1–2 show steadily increasing test error: CIFAR10 25.0→43.3→63.3→83.4%, CIFAR100 50.4→62.5→76.2→91.8%, and Tiny ImageNet 58.6→66.3→77.6→92.4%. This supports the test-error component only; rows are missing.
relationships.display_finding: Test error increased successively to 25.0%, 43.3%, 63.3%, and 83.4% on CIFAR10; 50.4%, 62.5%, 76.2%, and 91.8% on CIFAR100; and 58.6%, 66.3%, 77.6%, and 92.4% on Tiny ImageNet.

relationships.condition: Qualitative ResNet-32 logit trajectories on CIFAR10 with 40% label noise.
relationships.reason: Figure 2 and Section 3 show assigned logits growing above alternatives for clean examples, while the incorrect assigned logit remains below the ground-truth logit for most of training in mislabeled examples. This supports different learning dynamics; rows are missing.
relationships.display_finding: Assigned-label logits rose above alternatives for clean examples, while incorrect assigned-label logits stayed below true-label logits for most training on mislabeled examples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
